title: Vygotsky's Socio-Cultural Theory
summary: Vygotsky's theory: social interaction and culture in cognitive development, zone of proximal development (ZPD), scaffolding, more knowledgeable other (MKO) and cultural tools. Academic enrichment — no direct source coverage in Unit 09 PDFs.
objectives: Describe language as a cultural tool.
revision: Vygotsky's socio-cultural theory: ZPD, scaffolding, MKO, language as cultural tool. Editorial enrichment — not covered in Unit 09 PDFs.
traps: ZPD = alone vs with help gap.

notes.t: Lev Vygotsky proposed that cognitive development is shaped by social interaction, culture and language.
The gap between what a learner can do alone and what they can do with guidance.
Temporary support provided by a more knowledgeable person to help a learner master a task.
A person with more expertise who guides the learner (teacher, parent, peer).
Language is a cultural tool that mediates thought and development (private speech, inner speech).
UGC NET may ask about Vygotsky's ZPD, scaffolding and socio-cultural influences on development.

mnemonics.title: ZSM
mnemonics.text: Z — ZPD (gap: alone vs with help), S — Scaffolding (temporary support), M — MKO (more knowledgeable other)

flashcards.a: Development via social interaction, culture, language.
Gap between independent and assisted performance.
More knowledgeable other guides the learner.
